notes.6: Question 6 was answered correctly by 40 per cent who chose option C. 7 per cent chose option A, 45 per cent chose option B and 7 per cent chose option D. 1 per cent did not answer the question. A tax on a good would increase the cost of the good and shift the supply curve. Those candidates who chose option B recognised that demand would be likely to fall but as this fall was because of the rise in the price it would be shown on the diagram by a movement along the demand curve and not by a shift in the demand curve to D
notes.8: Question 8 was answered correctly by 35 per cent who chose option B. 39 per cent chose option A, 13 per cent chose option C and 13 per cent chose option D. Those candidates who chose option A may well have not noticed that the question asked what was not a market failure. Option A, external costs of production, is classified as a market failure. Similarly, over-consumption of de-merit goods and under-consumption of merit goods cause a misallocation of resources and are market failures. The only option that is not a market failure is B.
notes.16: Question 16 was answered correctly by 37 per cent who chose option C. 41 per cent chose option A, 17 per cent chose option B and 5 per cent chose option D. A government budget has both revenue and expenditure. Government revenue comes partly from taxation so the correct answer is indirect tax revenue.
notes.general_comments:
The questions for which most candidates selected the correct answer were 2, 4, 11, 13, 15, 19, 20, 23, 29
and 30. These questions were answered correctly by 75 per cent or more of the candidates. They covered
different parts of the syllabus and were set to test different skills.
The questions for which the fewest candidates selected the correct answer were 6, 8 and 16. These
questions were answered correctly by 40 per cent or fewer candidates. The rest of the questions gave
results which were well within the levels expected.
